It gives TWO Champions League league-phase tables side by side, and what separates them is the OPPONENT, not the round: 'PREISE UEFA CHAMPIONS LEAGUE GRUPPENPHASE FC BAYERN - CHELSEA FC' at 120 / 100 / 70 / 60 / 19 for categories 1 to 5, and 'PREISE UEFA CHAMPIONS LEAGUE GRUPPENPHASE FC BAYERN - BRUEGGE / SPORTING LISSABON / SAINT-GILLOISE' at 100 / 80 / 60 / 50 / 19. THE CATEGORY-5 CLUE WAS WORTHLESS, and why is worth keeping: 19 EUR is the Suedkurve standing price on every Champions League table on that page, and 15 EUR on every Bundesliga one. Category 5 agreeing between two Champions League sets therefore says only that both are Champions League - it would have matched whatever the two sets were. Use it to confirm a competition, never a round. PRICES DO RISE BY ROUND, so that half of the theory was right, and the same archive copy of the Jahreskarten page shows it for the season-ticket add-on: UCL Ligaphase 80/60/40/30/15, Achtelfinale 110/90/70/40/15, Viertelfinale and Halbfinale both 160/120/80/60/15. Those are Jahreskarten prices, a different product from these day-ticket rows, so they do not belong in these cells - but they are the evidence that a round-by-round ladder is real. WHAT IS NOW THE REAL PROBLEM WITH THESE ROWS: the page that matches them is the 2025|26 one, and these rows say 2026-27. fussball-tickets-kaufen.de, read directly on 2026-09-19, says the club has not published 26/27 league-phase prices at all. So these figures are most likely last season's, carried forward. They stand, because hand-written data wins, but the SEASON on them is unconfirmed and that is the cell to check. The 150/120/100/70/19 set was not found on any page read and is still unaccounted for.

ONE OBSERVED INSTANCE, NOT A STATED POLICY, and it contradicts the policy. Alexandru saw a Bundesliga ticket on the club's own member-only Zweitmarkt at around 120 EUR, against the 80 EUR category 1 face value above. The club's stated rule is the opposite: a resale price may not exceed face value. So one of three things is true and none has been checked - the 120 included VAT and fees on top of a compliant net price (80 EUR plus 19% is 95.20, so fees would have to be substantial), or it was a different category or a higher-priced fixture, or the ceiling is not enforced as stated. Recorded as seen, with the disagreement left in rather than argued away. priceBasis is unknown because it is not known whether the figure seen was gross or net. PARKED 2026-09-19, deliberately, and this is what it is waiting on: which market Alexandru actually saw the 120 EUR on. The club's own member-only Zweitmarkt inside the Digitalen Ticket Center and a general resale site are different claims - the face-value ceiling is the club's rule for its own market and says nothing about anybody else's. Until that is known another search is guesswork. One thing the archive read did add: the club's Jahreskarten pages treat the Zweitmarkt as a normal part of the Digitalen Ticket Center, and a listing there does NOT count towards a standing-place Jahreskarte's minimum-usage rule - so there is a real incentive to forward rather than sell, which is context for what does and does not get listed.
